commands.title: Print Directory Tree (Directories Only)
commands.description: Displays the directory structure of the current location while excluding files. Useful for quickly visualizing project folder organization.
commands.shortDescription: Shows directories only in a tree layout.
commands.exampleOutput:
.
├── src
│   ├── app
│   │   ├── api
│   │   └── dashboard
│   ├── components
│   └── styles
└── public
    └── images

6 directories
notes: Navigate to the target folder before running this command.
Requires the tree utility to be installed.

commands.title: Print Directory Tree with Files (2 Levels Deep)
commands.description: Displays the current directory structure including files while limiting the output depth to two directory levels. Useful for quickly inspecting a project's top-level organization.
commands.shortDescription: Shows project structure limited to two levels.
commands.exampleOutput:
.
├── README.md
├── next.config.mjs
├── package.json
├── public
│   ├── favicon.ico
│   └── images
├── src
│   ├── app
│   ├── components
│   └── styles
└── tsconfig.json

4 directories, 5 files
notes: Run from the target project directory.
The -L flag limits recursion depth.

commands.title: Print Directory Tree Excluding Junk Directories
commands.shortDescription: Shows a clean tree while ignoring generated folders.
commands.description: Displays the directory structure while excluding common generated folders, dependency directories, build output, and markdown files to produce a cleaner project overview.
commands.exampleOutput:
.
├── next.config.mjs
├── package.json
├── public
│   └── images
│       └── logo.png
├── src
│   ├── app
│   │   ├── layout.tsx
│   │   └── page.tsx
│   └── components
│       └── Button.tsx
└── tsconfig.json

4 directories, 6 files
notes: Excludes dependency folders and generated artifacts.
The ignore pattern syntax depends on the installed tree version.

commands.title: Print Directory Tree with Depth Limit and Exclusions
commands.shortDescription: Shows deeper architecture while excluding project noise.
commands.description: Generates a deeper project structure view while limiting recursion depth and filtering out unnecessary files. Useful for architectural inspection of larger applications.
commands.exampleOutput:
.
├── next.config.mjs
├── package.json
├── public
│   └── images
│       └── logo.png
├── src
│   ├── app
│   │   ├── dashboard
│   │   │   ├── settings
│   │   │   │   └── page.tsx
│   │   │   └── page.tsx
│   │   ├── layout.tsx
│   │   └── page.tsx
│   └── components
│       ├── Button.tsx
│       └── Card.tsx
└── tsconfig.json

6 directories, 9 files
notes: Useful for reviewing application architecture.
Increase or decrease the -L value depending on project size.

commands.title: Terminate All Node Processes
commands.shortDescription: Stops all running Node.js processes.
commands.description: Stops all running Node.js processes, including detached development servers, hanging npm scripts, and background Node workers.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ killall node
[1]+  Terminated              npm run dev
[2]+  Terminated              node server.js
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$
notes: This terminates all Node.js processes on the machine.
Use caution if multiple Node applications are running.

commands.title: Find and Remove node_modules Folders
commands.shortDescription: Finds and removes unused node_modules folders.
commands.description: Launches an interactive terminal interface for locating and deleting node_modules directories to recover disk space.
commands.exampleOutput:
npkill ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Scanning for node_modules...

  Path                                      Size       Last Mod
❯ /Projects/old-react-app/node_modules      412.3 MB   6 months ago
  /Projects/test-vite-project/node_modules  284.1 MB   2 weeks ago
  /Projects/sandbox/node_modules            310.5 MB   1 day ago

Total space that can be freed: 1.01 GB
Space freed: 0 B
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 [Space] Delete  [↓/↑] Move  [q] Quit
notes: Interactive command requiring user confirmation.
Deletes selected node_modules directories.

commands.title: Inspect ESLint Configuration
commands.shortDescription: Opens the ESLint configuration inspector.
commands.description: Launches the ESLint configuration inspector interface to visualize active rules, plugins, and flat configuration settings.
notes: Requires an inspect:linter script to exist in package.json.
Opens a browser-based inspection interface.

commands.title: Update npm Package Version Ranges
commands.shortDescription: Updates package versions in package.json.
commands.description: Updates package.json dependency versions to the latest available ranges while bypassing current semver constraints.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ npx npm-check-updates -u
Checking package.json dependencies...
[====================] 5/5 100%

 next           ^14.1.0  →  ^14.2.5
 react          ^18.2.0  →  ^18.3.1
 react-dom      ^18.2.0  →  ^18.3.1
 eslint         ^8.56.0  →  ^9.8.0
 typescript     ^5.3.3   →  ^5.5.4

Upgraded package.json
Run npm install to install new versions!
notes: Updates package.json only.
Run npm install afterward to install updated versions.
Review dependency changes before committing.

commands.title: Remove Extraneous npm Packages
commands.shortDescription: Removes packages not listed in package.json.
commands.description: Removes installed packages from node_modules that are not listed in package.json dependencies.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ npm prune
removed 14 packages, changed 1 package in 1.24s

audited 248 packages in 2s
found 0 vulnerabilities
notes: Useful after removing dependencies from package.json.
Synchronizes node_modules with declared dependencies.

commands.title: Launch Clean Chromium Instance
commands.shortDescription: Launches a clean Chromium testing session.
commands.description: Launches a clean Chromium browser instance from the terminal using a temporary environment without existing cookies, history, or browser extensions interfering with testing.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ npx @rnx-kit/chromium-edge-launcher
Launching clean Chromium instance...
Target debugging port opened on: http://127.0.0.1:9222
Press Ctrl+C to close browser session and clear temporary profile metadata.
notes: Creates a clean browser session isolated from the local browser profile.
Requires Node.js and npm/npx availability.

commands.title: Generate Secure Random Hex Key
commands.shortDescription: Generates a secure random hexadecimal key.
commands.description: Generates a cryptographically secure random hexadecimal string suitable for environment secrets, encryption salts, and application keys.
notes: Requires OpenSSL to be installed.
Increase byte length for stronger secrets when required.

commands.title: Clear Next.js Build Cache
commands.shortDescription: Clears the Next.js build cache.
commands.description: Deletes the Next.js generated build directory and local cache files to resolve stale builds, outdated bundles, and development server inconsistencies.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ rm -rf .next
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ npm run dev

> next-app@0.1.0 dev
> next dev

   ▲ Next.js 15.0.0
   - Local:        http://localhost:3000

 ✓ Starting...
 ✓ Ready in 1400ms
notes: Deletes generated build output.
Requires restarting the Next.js development server afterward.
Command is destructive for the targeted directory.

commands.title: Deep Clean Git Untracked Files
commands.shortDescription: Deletes ignored and untracked Git files.
commands.description: Removes all untracked files and directories from a Git repository, including ignored files such as build artifacts, dependencies, and local environment files.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ git clean -fdx
Removing .env.local
Removing .next/
Removing node_modules/
Removing out/
notes: Highly destructive command.
Can delete .env files, node_modules, and generated artifacts.
Use git clean -fdxn first to preview changes.

commands.title: Interactively Update npm Dependencies
commands.shortDescription: Interactively updates npm dependencies.
commands.description: Runs taze to interactively review and update outdated npm dependencies with selective package upgrade control.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ npx taze -r
taze v0.13.0

  dependencies
  ❯ next          14.2.0  →  15.0.0   (major)
    react         18.2.0  →  19.0.0   (major)

  devDependencies
  ❯ eslint         8.57.0  →  9.12.0   (major)

  [Space] Toggle  [Enter] Select  [A] All  [Q] Abort
notes: Interactive terminal application.
Review major version updates carefully.

commands.title: Find Unused and Missing Dependencies
commands.shortDescription: Finds unused and missing dependencies.
commands.description: Analyzes a project to identify unused dependencies and packages referenced in code but missing from package.json.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ npx depcheck
Unused dependencies
* lodash
* dotenv
Missing dependencies
* lucide-react (used in src/components/Button.tsx)
notes: Useful before production releases.
May report false positives for dynamically loaded dependencies.

commands.title: Modern Directory Tree with eza
commands.shortDescription: Displays a modern colored directory tree.
commands.description: Uses eza to display a modern directory tree with file icons, colors, and enhanced filesystem visualization.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ eza --tree --level=2
.
├── 📄 README.md
├── ⚙️ next.config.mjs
├── 📦 package.json
├── 📂 public
│   ├── 🖼️ favicon.ico
│   └── 📂 images
├── 📂 src
│   ├── 📂 app
│   ├── 📂 components
│   └── 📂 styles
└── ⚙️ tsconfig.json
notes: Requires eza to be installed.
Modern alternative to tree with additional visual features.

commands.title: Search Project Files with ripgrep
commands.shortDescription: Searches project files using ripgrep.
commands.description: Searches text across an entire project directory using ripgrep, providing extremely fast results while respecting .gitignore exclusions.
notes: Automatically respects .gitignore files.
Faster alternative to grep for source code searching.
Requires ripgrep to be installed.

commands.title: Analyze Disk Usage Interactively
commands.shortDescription: Analyzes disk usage interactively.
commands.description: Launches an interactive terminal disk usage analyzer for identifying large folders, caches, and hidden storage consumers.
notes: Interactive disk explorer.
Useful when cleanup tools like npkill are not enough.
Requires gdu availability.

commands.title: Inspect Process Using Network Port
commands.shortDescription: Finds processes using a network port.
commands.description: Displays processes currently listening on a specific network port, including process IDs and application details.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~/my-nextjs-app$ lsof -i :3000
COMMAND   PID USER   FD   TYPE DEVICE SIZE/OFF NODE NAME
node    84321 user   23u  IPv6  0x1234      0t0  TCP *:3000 (LISTEN)
notes: Useful for finding processes blocking development ports.
Combine with kill command to terminate identified processes.

commands.title: Generate Multiple UUID Values
commands.command: for i in {1..5}; do uuidgen; done
commands.shortDescription: Generates multiple UUID values.
commands.description: Runs a shell loop that generates multiple UUID values using the system uuidgen utility.
commands.exampleOutput:
user@machine:~$ for i in {1..5}; do uuidgen; done
6e67cf3d-fa3e-46a4-bb23-fa5da2a98f1a
30335e23-28f0-4660-8f96-3a7cbef95393
d7d2427a-5f04-4c6e-b34e-52f1908bf41a
837ef390-349c-482a-a9e9-74d110da2df4
1e791b8d-29cb-4be8-8db9-8b851ad5ccbe
notes: Change the loop number to generate more or fewer UUID values.
Requires uuidgen availability on the host system.
